text:
sahil: Heads-up — seeing rows from other workspaces in a saved query on prod console after the quick-switch rollout. Screenshot: https://redwood.app/s/shot (blurred). Not a one-off, a whole section shows org B's snippets in org A's view.
maya: ugh saw something similar on QA after enabling quick-switch-optim. Thought it was stale prefetch but this looks like real cross-org bleed. :face_with_raised_eyebrow:
alex: Can you paste the network/request? my gut says missing org header when we hit the decorated cache.
sahil: paste logs + request dump:
```
POST /graphql 200
Headers: {
  "Authorization": "Bearer xxxxxx",
  "Accept": "application/json"
}
Body: {
  "query": "query SavedItems($workspaceId: ID!) { savedItems(workspaceId: $workspaceId) { id title owner } }",
  "variables": {"workspaceId": "org-A-1"}
}
Logs: cache_hit=true cache_key=session:usr-42:dashboard:savedquery org_header=""
```
jamie: that cache_key is the problem — decorator caches by session not by workspace. If session is reused across orgs (quick-switch flow) you will surface the wrong rows. We added the session-based key to speed up cold starts in April.
alex: also noticed telemetry: some requests show `org_id=null` in prod traces which means gateway didn't set org from header. If gateway falls back to user's default org, combined with session-keyed cache you'll leak.
maya: immediate mitigation: flip the flag for quick-switch-optim off and invalidate dashboard savedquery cache keys. Longer fix: include workspace in cache key + enforce X-Workspace header at gateway.
sahil: agree. Who can flip flag + run invalidate? @deploy-bot do we have a maintenance window for quick toggle rollback?
deploy-bot: rolled back feature flag `quick-switch-optim` to OFF in prod at 2026-03-20T11:08:00Z. CI run: https://ci.redwood/rollouts/7654
alex: thanks. I'd also like to add a defensive invariant at graphql-gateway: if body.variables.workspaceId != header X-Workspace then log an alert and return 400. That prevents silent mis-scoped queries from hitting caches.
jamie: yes, adding workspace to cache key is also necessary. current code:
```
const key = `session:${userId}:dashboard:savedquery`;
```
proposed:
```
const key = `session:${userId}:workspace:${workspaceId}:dashboard:savedquery`;
```
sahil: can we also add a telemetry rule to surface `org_mismatch` when header vs body org differ? We missed this in rollout smoke tests.
maya: will open PRs: one for gateway header enforcement + telemetry alert, one for decorator cache-key change. I'll include a migration to expire old keys.
alex: quick note — if we change cache key shape we should run a short job to invalidate the old ones in redis to avoid high memory churn. Jamie, can your team handle that script?
jamie: yep, will write a small ttl/scan job to evict `session:*:dashboard:savedquery` keys after rollout. I'll coordinate on timing.
sahil: ok action items: 1) maya flips flag (done by deploy-bot). 2) jamie run eviction job (T+30min). 3) maya submit PRs (gateway + decorator) targeted for canary next week. 4) alex adds telemetry dashboard for org_mismatch and sets alert at 5/min.
alex: also want a short postmortem note pinned in incidents channel once we verify root cause and fixes rolled out.
maya: adding to my todo list. I'll post PR links in this thread when ready.
sahil: thanks all. after deploy-bot rollback I rechecked the problematic org — instances are gone. Keeping thread open until PRs merged and eviction done.
deploy-bot: maintenance note: feature flag rollback succeeded, no database migrations required. Canary traffic routed back to baseline.
maya: updated: created PRs: https://git.redwood/p/frontend/1234 (decorator cache key), https://git.redwood/p/gateway/4321 (header enforcement + telemetry). Will request reviews.
jamie: eviction job queued, running at 11:45 UTC. will post logs when finished.
sahil: great. once both PRs are merged let's do a tightly scoped canary with telemetry guardrails before re-enabling the quick-switch optimization.
